event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: A line-by-line review of the 2023 Form 10-K excerpt reveals no direct or even indirect acknowledgement of the COVID-19 pandemic, its lingering effects, or any explicit discussion of pandemic-driven supply-chain disruption, labour shortages, remote work, or altered customer-demand patterns.  The risk-factor and MD&A sections instead reference general ‘supply-chain constraints’ and ‘tight labour-market conditions’ without attributing them to COVID-19 or any other public-health emergency.  Because the filing date (27 Feb 2024) falls well within three years of the height of the COVID-19 shock, an explicit disclosure would normally merit a high risk score under the Time Decay Principle.  However, the company’s silence on the topic means that, in effect, SRE is providing the market with no COVID-specific transparency.  The absence of language is itself a governance signal, yet strictly under the scoring framework there is no extractable sentence to which a positive or negative risk weight can be attached.  Consequently, there is no evidence to score, and the overall pandemic-related risk evidence level is assessed as non-existent for this document.
